title: F6.1: Implement — Implement mount create/list/show/update/delete commands
description: Implement this feature according to its parent acceptance criteria and the approved design. Keep mount configuration changes distinct from artifact content changes.
design: Manage [[mounts]] in the configured TOML file, without registry access. Add required `--config FILE` to the mount command group (`mount --config FILE create|list|show|update|delete`). `create NAME` takes --prefix, --registry, --repository, optional --root-tag and repeatable --redirect-allowlist; it may initialize a missing/version-only config. `update NAME` applies explicitly supplied --prefix/--registry/--repository/--root-tag fields; --reset-root-tag and --clear-redirect-allowlist enable clearing, while repeated --redirect-allowlist replaces the list. Mount name is immutable. `list` emits a JSON array, `show` one JSON object, mutations emit JSON status/record. Use toml_edit DocumentMut to preserve unrelated comments/formatting, then validate the complete serialized config with Config::parse before writing. Writes use a same-directory tempfile, sync and atomic persist, reject symlink/non-regular config targets, and preserve existing permissions. Deleting the last mount is rejected because service configuration requires at least one. Errors are actionable and no command contacts a registry.

title: Prevent lost updates in concurrent mount configuration mutations
description: Independent F6.3 audit of 8cc8fd1b8b5525564ffa81161fd8d42a929f8ae0 found that atomic_write compares the current config with the original, then unconditionally persists the tempfile. Two mount commands can both pass the comparison before either rename, so the later rename silently overwrites the earlier update. Serialize mutations or use a robust conflict strategy that closes the compare-to-persist window. Add a deterministic concurrent-writer regression test that proves both non-conflicting updates are retained or one fails with MountConfigChanged, and compiled-binary checks for the registry field in mutation JSON plus version-only initialization and symlink/non-regular target refusal where portable. The existing race test changes the file before validation and does not cover this interleaving.
notes: Fixed the audit finding. All mount create/update/delete mutations now acquire an exclusive fs2 advisory lock on a persistent hidden sidecar adjacent to the config before reading, validating, and writing; canonicalized parent directories make common path aliases share the lock. Lock is released by OS on process exit. Existing compare-before-persist check remains for external non-locking edits. Added deterministic lock-exclusion and simultaneous-update unit coverage, plus a compiled-binary two-process test that holds the config lock, verifies both commands stay blocked, releases it, then verifies both distinct updates survive. Added compiled CLI checks for registry JSON output, version-only initialization, and nonregular/symlink refusal. Full default, real-registry, fmt, clippy, build, docs, and diff gates all pass in working tree; commit/review follows.
close_reason: Cross-process config mutations are serialized and covered by deterministic lock-exclusion, concurrent-update unit, and compiled CLI process tests. F6.3 independent re-review is still required before closing its audit gate.

title: Bound concurrent HTTP requests and in-flight streams
description: The F7.3 audit observed that the HTTP listener has no application-level concurrency cap. Each routed request can hold registry work or an upstream-to-client response stream, so a burst or many slow clients may consume unbounded tasks and sockets. Add configurable request concurrency and operational timeouts without logging secrets.
acceptance_criteria: A configured cap prevents excess requests from opening registry work and returns a generic 503 response before claiming success. The permit remains held through response-body completion or client disconnect, then is released. Request/registry and idle-stream timeout behavior is explicit and bounded. Real-listener tests use a local registry or narrowly injected slow stream, prove saturation and permit recovery, and ensure Authorization values remain absent from logs.
notes:
Non-blocking P2 finding from independent F7.3 audit of routing revision 19d3d0223179706f297b20f30e85f5880f0aa7da. Reviewer noted axum::serve has no active-request/stream concurrency cap; this is important before exposing a non-loopback listener. The separate R6 low-resource resilience work may coordinate implementation.
Also recorded by the independent F8.3 audit of c7ce03e4cf7432e5e6dcd89d9402c4083b2af625: ADR 0002 §6 still requires configurable request/registry/idle timeouts and a concurrency limit that accounts for in-flight streams. This remains non-blocking for F8 static semantics but is required before public non-loopback deployment.
F10.1 auth-safe directory listing preflights every registry-backed page into an unnamed temporary file before 200 headers, so a late page 401 can still be relayed correctly. This preflight adds resource/lifecycle work that must be included in this issue: bound per-listing spool bytes and aggregate concurrent spool storage, retain request permits through final spool response, and bound registry traversal/idle time; cancellation should stop preflight traversal and delete temporary state. Do not expose non-loopback until these limits are implemented/tested.
F10 audit follow-up coverage now proves a configured-registry 401 injected during a later autoindex page returns 401/challenge before 200 headers (real registry plus narrow FaultProxy injection; test `serve_maps_a_late_autoindex_page_challenge_before_committing_success_headers`). Remaining hip scope is resource lifecycle: cap spool bytes and aggregate concurrency, bound/cancel preflight traversal, and ensure cleanup; no non-loopback exposure until those limits pass.

title: Bound OCI directory index traversal depth
description: The independent F4.3 audit noted that path depth is capped, but directory index pages are recursively followed without an explicit structural-depth cap.
